blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: The first plan needs 45 crew-weeks and the season has 48. Why does the lesson not settle for one crew row over the whole season?

options.text: The 45 crew-weeks include trims the budget already refuses
options.says: The first plan is within the budget; every trim in it is affordable.

options.text: Three long trims would push the plan past the season's 48
options.says: The plan's total is 45, which is below 48.

options.text: Crews are booked by month, and each month must hold its own work
options.says: Right: fitting work into months is a packing problem that season totals cannot answer.

options.text: A row over the whole season cannot be written in a MILP
options.says: The options table writes it as one row; it is rejected because it passes plans no month can hold.

origin.section: The Knapsack Cannot See Time or Crews

questions.stem: In another optimal month plan, C12 moves from month 1 to month 6 and nothing else changes. What happens to the objective value?

options.text: Nothing, since the objective counts risk whatever the month
options.says: Right: moving C12 from month 1 to month 6 removes the same risk.

options.text: It falls, since a trim late in the season removes less risk
options.says: The month model's objective has no month in it; that is the next lesson's change.

options.text: It rises, since month 6 has more crew-weeks left to fill
options.says: The objective counts risk removed, not crew-weeks; the move removes the same risk.

options.text: It falls by C12's share of the month 6 crew capacity
options.says: The objective counts risk removed, which the move leaves unchanged.

origin.section: The Crews Change the Plan: Two Circuits Out, Two In

questions.stem: Two of the new tests use the same circuits A and B (3 crew-weeks each) and one crew, once with one month and once with two. Why the pair?

options.text: So the budget, not the crews, decides between A and B
options.says: The budget is $1,000k, money for both; the crews decide.

options.text: Because each circuit needs more crew-weeks than a month holds
options.says: Each needs 3 crew-weeks and one crew's month holds 4.

options.text: Because a second month doubles the risk each trim removes
options.says: The objective counts risk whatever the month.

options.text: So a model with no crew rows fails: one refused, one allowed
options.says: Right: a refused and an allowed case from the same circuits catch a model that ignores the crews.

origin.section: Three Tests State the Crew Rule

concepts: what a month model scores when trims move
why crew tests come in allowed and refused pairs
why crew capacity is stated month by month
